reviews.text: I had made an appointment for a combination vaccine injection, but they gave my dog ​​a rabies shot without my consent. I only realized what had happened after the doctor had given the shot without checking, saying, "Next time it'll be the combination vaccine." When I asked, "Then what did you just give your dog?", they said it was rabies. What's more, that shot had only been given a month earlier during a mass vaccination, and despite the significant strain on my dog's body, they didn't even apologize when I pointed it out. I opened Google Maps to make an appointment at another hospital and this hospital's name came up, which reminded me of my anger, so I'm writing this. The doctor is the short-haired man pictured. Their response after the problem occurred was as if I were a complainer; they didn't apologize at all, and even when I asked to speak to a supervisor, they never appeared. I never received an apology or letter from the male doctor until the very end. Don't call yourself a doctor.

Dear Nana,
Thank you for your kind review. We will continue to strive to provide a wide range of treatment options and warm service so that many patients can visit us with peace of mind. Please feel free to contact us anytime if you have any further concerns.

Staff of Motoazabu Animal Medical Center

The Animal Hospital Center is a truly wonderful hospital, overflowing with love for animals and humanity, thanks to the amazing Director Kawasaki and the other doctors, as well as the nurses.
With a large staff, they sincerely address any symptoms, providing the best medical care and demonstrating proactive action based on a spirit of hospitality. I am truly grateful to have found the Motoazabu Animal Medical Center. Below are the details.

------------------------------
My 11-year-old female cat (Amo) suddenly cried out and wriggled one morning, and we rushed her to the Motoazabu Animal Hospital Center.
She was diagnosed with restrictive cardiomyopathy and hydroplegia, and given only 1-2 months to live, or at most 2 years. After repeated hospitalizations and discharges, thanks to the attentive care of the doctors and nurses at the center, our beloved cat quickly adapted to the center.

Everyone's love for animals was truly wonderful, and their sincere and compassionate approach to dogs, cats, and their families was incredibly reassuring and invaluable.

Given the difficulty of achieving a complete cure for this illness, we were filled with gratitude for the attentive care provided by Dr. Kawasaki, the head of the clinic, and all the other doctors and nurses.

For about a month and a half after the diagnosis, everyone worked together and gave their all. Our daughter has now crossed the rainbow bridge, but I believe she is truly grateful to everyone at the Animal Medical Center.

This center also has doctors who speak native English, so many patients from overseas visit.

Amo's twin sister is still living happily, so we will of course entrust her future health checkups and care to the Animal Medical Center Motoazabu (which will be moving to Nishiazabu from late September).

This is a veterinary hospital that values ​​its relationships and fosters mutual trust.

Fortunately, it was located not too far from my home, so they were able to provide daily house calls.

Immediately after my pet's passing, they offered condolences and even placed flowers – such thoughtful consideration.

I express my heartfelt gratitude to Director Kawasaki and everyone else. Thank you. T.K.

My senior Border Collie is a patient here. His kidney function has worsened, so we've been taking him in for regular checkups. Following the doctor's advice, and referencing books on senior dog nutrition, we've modified his homemade diet to avoid worsening his kidney disease, and he's still very healthy. I believe we've been able to significantly slow the progression of his condition thanks to the doctor. I'm also very grateful for the doctor's ability to quickly identify any signs of other serious illnesses and for always providing clear and thorough explanations. Furthermore, as he's aged, his hind legs have weakened. He would sit down if I simply placed my hand under his hips during shampooing, his hips would sag from side to side when he walked, he dragged his leg slightly, and he walked slowly. Though I'm not a medical professional, I thought that strengthening his muscles might improve his condition, so I took him to the rehabilitation specialist clinic. After a thorough consultation on the first visit, the doctor deeply addressed the problematic areas and performed myofascial release, and it was remarkably effective from the very first treatment. His hind legs have straightened, his walking speed has increased, and he can now walk at the same pace as us. Also, before treatment, when we removed his collar, his hind legs would stiffen up along with it, but that has completely stopped. The fascia is always connected, so it seems that the release has prevented it from being pulled. Previously, he would urinate with both hind legs on the ground, but now he can lift one leg like when he was younger, and his hind leg core has become stronger. He can now stand firmly without sitting or wobbling when lightly touched on the waist. Perhaps because his body feels lighter, he also wakes up more easily. We understand that his muscles are still stiff, so we would like to continue treatment. Thanks to the excellent treatment by the doctor, our elderly dog ​​has become younger, and we are truly grateful. The nurses and staff are also efficient, always cheerful and kind, and we are so glad to have found such a good hospital.

I want to leave a sincere thankful review to the doctors at Motoazabu. We arrived to Japan around 8 months ago with our two cats and had to find a reliable clinic. English speaking staff is a great plus because my Japanese is far from perfect.
So far we've done a complete health check and vaccinations for our two furry babies, a dental workup for the older one, had an emergency visit with the younger one and currently treating dermatitis. I have nothing but positive impressions to share. The staff is very nice, I can tell that they truly love pets and take the best care of them! A separate appreciation goes out for always calming down the anxious owner (me)!
We are very happy we've found this clinic but still hope that we won't need to visit often and the cats will remain healthy.

Whenever someone asks for a recommendation on a good veterinarian office in the Minato, or Roppongi area or in Tokyo in general, I get excited to tell them about our veterinary office.

Of course there is sometimes a language barrier with my Japanese not being strong yet but they are always eager to use a translator with me and my husband and even have English speaking veterinarians working some days and a lot of them that are eager and working to learn the language. Do Not let this stop you.

When we moved to Japan, we moved here with our 2 year old French bulldog, Gus. My moon, my pride and joy. That being said it was one of the things I was most nervous about for moving across the world to a new country; what the veterinarian service and situation would be like. Of course it didn’t take long for us to need a veterinarian, for a routine check up and wow am I glad that we found these amazing humans. I always thought that our veterinarians were good in the United States but these professionals go above and beyond to a level I have never experienced every single time we visit them and always give the best care. You can truly tell that they love their job and love being around all animals.

Since we have been here about 9 months now, we have added another French bulldog to our family and they have given her, Kuma-bear, exceptional care since arriving. I could go on and on about my experiences with these people but there is no one I trust more with my dogs than these amazing people. We love and appreciate every single one of them, we are So thankful that they exist.

We have gone in from everything from routine check ups, vaccinations, conversations about surgery and I have never felt so comfortable. I will leave you with this; on our daily walks, Gus will drag me to the vet and stop and stare inside. Both dogs Love these people and this veterinary office! 🫶🫶🐶🐶❤️❤️

My pet almost died because of treatment at this hospital. The doctor was an amateur; when I asked questions about the illness, he hesitantly gave nonsensical opinions. When I told him I was a medical professional, he gave only superficial explanations, didn't know the name of the illness, and kept recommending pointless, expensive tests. My trust in him completely crumbled, and my pet's life was saved by transferring to another hospital.

The doctor in charge was the female hospital director.

I only went there because it was close, but I will never go back.
I went for my first check-up. Everyone was very kind, the examination went smoothly, and I think it's a trustworthy animal hospital!

On January 27th, Dr. Isono at Kotakibashi Animal Hospital performed surgery for bilateral patellar luxation, and Dr. Ogasawara at Motoazabu Animal Medical Center provided rehabilitation until April 4th.
Dr. Ogasawara treated my dog ​​with laser therapy to improve blood flow, checked the movement of both legs, and gave massages, and my dog ​​seemed to enjoy it, squinting his eyes in pleasure!
The doctors at the group hospitals shared all of my dog's medical records, which gave me great peace of mind.
Although it was a bit of a distance from Asagaya Pet Clinic Satellite where my dog ​​was hospitalized to Motoazabu, we were able to stop by a pet-friendly restaurant in Roppongi Hills, which was nearby, on the way back from rehabilitation, and it was a lot of fun!
Thank you to all the doctors and staff for your care.
